Rafiq Ghattas, who lives in the Mina camp, home to around 1,700 families, said conditions deteriorated within an hour of the rain starting. #freepalestine🇵🇸❤️ #palistanegaza #rek #fyp #foryou The question of Palestine is one of the most complex and painful issues in modern world politics. The Palestinian cause is not merely a territorial dispute — it touches on questions of justice, human rights, and national self-determination. The slogan "Free Palestine" has become a symbol of the Palestinian people's aspiration for freedom, dignity, and their own statehood. Understanding this issue requires examining its historical roots, the current humanitarian situation, the legal framework, and the arguments of all sides. Historical Context The modern history of Palestine begins with the collapse of the Ottoman Empire after World War I, when the territory came under British administration through a League of Nations mandate. In 1917, the Balfour Declaration expressed British support for a "national home for the Jewish people" in Palestine, while also stating that the rights of existing non-Jewish communities should not be prejudiced. In 1947, the United Nations adopted Resolution 181, proposing the partition of Palestine into separate Jewish and Arab states, with Jerusalem under international administration. The Jewish leadership accepted the plan; the Arab leadership rejected it. In 1948, the State of Israel was declared, triggering the first Arab-Israeli war. Around 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled — an event Palestinians call the Nakba, meaning "catastrophe."

Every road leads to a dead end. “Where am I supposed to go?” a Palestinian man cries after Israeli occupation warplanes flattened his house and workshop near the Jordanian Hospital in Gaza City’s Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood. Nothing reached his family for free, he says. Not the tent, not the tarps, not even the water jugs. They paid for all of it, scraping the money together while living in a tent, and now the strike has taken what little they had left. The UN-led Shelter Cluster says Gaza needs around 121,000 tents, 561,000 tarps and 1.7 million mattresses to get through winter, yet as of November 5 there were only about 2,800 tents, 76,000 tarps and fewer than 5,000 mattresses inside the Strip, and not a single emergency shelter kit. More than 150,000 tents are sitting outside Gaza waiting for the Israeli occupation’s approval, and the International Organization for Migration says its shelter kits keep being turned away at the crossings as “dual-use” items. Supplies cover barely 17 percent of winter shelter needs, and Save the Children says winter clothing covers just 1 percent. While families wait for aid that never comes, the airstrikes keep coming. @khaled.sulttan

videos.caption: Why is Gaza drowning? Images of floods engulfing Gaza have gone viral. Most coverage focuses on the humanitarian catastrophe. Few explain what caused it. Since October 2023, Israeli forces have destroyed nearly all of Gaza’s infrastructure. Up to 68 million tons of rubble now blanket the Strip. Homes, schools, hospitals, and basic services have been flattened, with at least 90 percent of the territory destroyed. Now, as winter sets in, the first rains are making what is left unlivable. At least five people have been killed after sand embankments collapsed in the downpour. None of this is new. The Israeli plan to make Gaza unlivable has been unfolding for years. In 2012, the UN warned that Gaza could be unlivable by 2020 because of repeated Israeli assaults, a crippling blockade, the collapse of its aquifer, energy shortages, and mass unemployment. Despite the so-called ceasefire, our reporter in Gaza describes a situation that is impossible to endure: no shelter, no aid, and a ban on rebuilding. Conditions are getting worse by the day.” @specter_affairs
